articles.title: When Morningness Is Confused with Godliness
articles.summary: Could it be possible that our idealizing of morning quiet times is more cultural than biblical?
articles.summary_zh: 我们对早晨安静时间的理想化是否比圣经更具文化性？
articles.content: “Do your quiet time with God every morning.” “Give God your first hours (your best hours!) of the day.” “Rise early for Scripture and prayer; it sets the tone for the rest of your day!” From pulpits to podcasts, I’ve heard these sentiments often in Christian circles. The instructions aren’t just to spend alone time with God but to specifically do so as the very first act of your day. For many, the “morning quiet time” has become a measuring rod of how well you’re doing in your relationship with God. Actor Mark Wahlberg once went viral on Instagram for a screenshot of his morning routine : waking up at 2:30 a.m., praying at 2:45, and completing his first workout before 5:30. This is one of many examples of how early rising has become associated with aspirational godliness. But is it really more virtuous to be a morning person than a night owl? What If You Have to Sleep In? Behind the modern mindset of hyperidealized mornings is the assumption that being a “morning person” is a virtue in and of itself—a gritty choice toward wellness and productivity within everyone’s power. The implication is that if you’re disciplined and wise, you’ll set the alarm clock and start the day early; you’ll make it happen. If you’re slothful or foolish, you won’t. Extenuating circumstances are just excuses. For many, the ‘morning quiet time’ has become a measuring rod of how well you’re doing in your relationship with God. But what would this mean for nurses whose work begins and ends when it’s dark outside? What about parents with newborns, whose babies’ demands don’t abide by our ideal rhythms? How about Christians who are naturally night owls: most alert, focused, and productive at night? Should these folks just suck it up and aspire to get up earlier in spite of their circumstances? Or could it be possible that our idealizing of morning quiet times is more cultural than biblical? God Loves Early Risers At first glance, it might seem that God’s Word does value our mornings most. Pastor David Mathis wrote an insightful article summarizing the abundance of instances in Scripture in which God’s people (including Christ himself!) either rose early to good effect or were directed by God to do so. Consider the Psalms: In Psalm 5:3, David says, “O LORD, in the morning you hear my voice.” In Psalm 88:13, the Sons of Korah sing, “In the morning my prayer comes before you.” In Psalm 90:14, Moses prays to God, “Satisfy us in the morning with your steadfast love, that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.” God clearly meets with his people in the morning. Case closed? Not quite. When you consult the whole counsel of Scripture, it becomes clear that God emphasizes meditating on his Word, singing his praises, and praying to his name just as much in the night as in the morning. Nocturnal Worship Let’s explore some nighttime examples. In Acts 16:25–26, after Paul and Silas are imprisoned in Philippi, God’s Word notably mentions the timing of their worship: “About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God . . .” Silas and Paul don’t try to go to sleep early so they can engage with God at the crack of dawn. They stay up late, worshiping at midnight. The results are profound. In Psalm 63:5–6, David prays to the Lord, “My soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips, when I remember you upon my bed, and meditate on you in the watches of the night.” This psalm as a whole is arguably a nighttime prayer. David prays these lyrics to the Lord seemingly all while on his “bed,” singing midnight praises. Consider Jesus’s earthly life. On the fateful day before his crucifixion, when it comes to spending devoted time alone with his Father, Jesus prays passionately, in Gethsemane, at night (Matt. 26:36–56). There is no mention in the Gospels of Jesus rising early on this momentous day; it might have happened, but the recorded emphasis is Jesus’s spiritual devotion in the dark. Morning and evening aren’t

每天早晨,你应当与真主在一起。 你们当在白昼中为真主而初次。 你应当为天经和拜功而早起,它为你的其余的日子而定调。 我经常在基督教圈子里听到这些情绪, 这些指示不仅仅是要独自与上帝相处,

对许多人来说,“早晨的宁静时间”已经成为衡量你与上帝关系如何的尺度。 演员Mark Wahlberg曾经在Instagram上病毒化, 这是许多例子之一,说明早起如何与渴望的虔诚联系在一起。

但做个早起的人 比做个夜猫子更善良吗? 如果你必须睡觉呢? 现今的极端理想化的晨光思想背后的假设是,作为一个“晨光的人”本身就是一种美德——一种在每个人的力量范围内对健康和生产力的粗鲁选择。

也就是说,如果你有纪律和智慧,你就会设置警钟,早起;你会让它发生。 如果你懒惰或愚蠢, 减轻罪责只是借口 对许多人来说,`早晨的平静时间'已成为衡量你与上帝关系如何的尺度。

但对于工作开始和结束的护士来说, 有新生儿的父母, 其婴儿的要求不符合我们的理想节奏, 自然是夜猫子的基督徒:最警觉,最专注,最有成果的夜晚,怎么样? 这些人是否应该吸了它,渴望早起,不管他们的情况如何?

或者,我们理想化的清晨平静时期,是否比圣经更具有文化色彩? 神爱早起者 乍一看,上帝的言语似乎对我们的早晨最为重要。

大卫·马西斯牧师写了一篇富有洞察力的文章,总结了圣经中大量的例子,其中上帝的子民(包括基督本人)不是早起,就是奉上帝指示这样做。

你看看《古兰经》吧!在《古兰经》5:3中,大卫说: 耶和華啊!你在早晨听见我的声音。 在"诗经"第88:13中,可拉之子们唱道:"早晨,我的祈祷降临你们面前". 在《诗经》第90章第14节中,穆萨祈祷真主说:我们早晨以你们的坚忍的慈爱来安慰我们,以便我们快乐地度过我们的日子。 早晨,上帝显然与他的人相会。 结案? 没有

articles.title: ‘Young Man, You Look Miserable’
articles.summary: God changed the heart of a young “prince of preachers” all with a single, simple verse: Look to Jesus and live. Watch Now
articles.summary_zh: 神用一句简单的诗句改变了一位年轻的“传道者之王”的心：仰望耶稣，活下去。现在观看
articles.content: I’m excited to tell you the story of how God used a simple verse, from a complicated passage, to change the life of a man named Charles Spurgeon. His story is for everyone, but it may have a special word to speak to a few groups in the room. One is laymen — that is, people who work for a living in normal jobs, outside of Christian ministry. People without a seminary education, people who aren’t pastors or have ministry jobs. We recognize that this series has profiled four men who were preachers. Now, there is an interesting flow to our series: - first, Saint Augustine, - then, Luther, who was an Augustinian monk, - then, John Bunyan, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Luther’s commentary on Galatians, - now, Charles Spurgeon, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress. We’ve moved from one convert to another, each building in some way on the previous one, but a weakness of our series (in some sense) is that they all became preachers. And we don’t expect you all to become preachers; we’d like a few, but most will be laymen, and that’s good. Now, Spurgeon is known as “the Prince of Preachers.” But the hero, under God, in Spurgeon’s story is not Spurgeon, and not a trained, paid preacher, but a layman. So, Spurgeon’s story has a special word for laymen who are willing to open their mouths and say what they know about Jesus. Spurgeon’s story also has a special word for teens and young adults. Spurgeon came to faith at age fifteen, which in his day was far more like young adulthood. Still, his story offers a challenge to those who are no longer children and not yet established adults: teens, college students, grad students, even young professionals. Don’t let the world (or the church) lower your standards of what’s possible in being deeply converted and dedicated to Jesus — and how God can make his Son thrilling to a young soul. My prayer is that God might be pleased to give some their own engine. So often, parents, college workers, and pastors help young adults along and give them pushes. And then sometimes, God is pleased in the life of teenagers to give them their own engine, and they don’t need any more pushing. They say, “Get out of my way! I am going to follow Jesus. You can’t keep me from him and worship, my Bible, and prayer!” That’s what God did for Spurgeon at age fifteen — he gave him his own engine. And I pray he might be pleased to do that even here this morning. Spurgeon’s story speaks to one more group: those in the room who are willing to admit, “I’m here but I’m not saved.” For two thousand years, unsaved people have shown up at churches for all sorts of reasons. That’s Spurgeon’s story. He was searching. He was unsaved and in a church on a Sunday morning when God broke through. So, if you’d say this morning, “I haven’t settled the issue of my sin and rebellion against God,” or “I haven’t ‘been saved,’” or “if I died on the drive home today, I wouldn’t be at peace with my Maker,” this story has a special word for you. So, let me tell you about Charlie Spurgeon. His Early and Whole Life He was born in 1834, about 40 miles northeast of London, into a Christian family. In fact, both his father and grandfather were pastors. But his father met financial troubles and sent the young Charles to live with his grandparents from ages one to six. I don’t think this is an insignificant part of the story; don’t underestimate the effects of a good grandma and grandpa in the lives of our children. From their influence he emerged as “precocious,” learned to read, and first found Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (which he would read more than a hundred times). From his earliest days, he was unusually sharp, ahead of his age level, “always reading books” (Spurgeon: A Biography, 8). He returned home at age six and excelled at school in both math and reading. He was noticed for “his unusual mental ability and his rare clarity of speech” (10), including “his native audacity” (11), that is, his courage to say
articles.content_zh:
我非常兴奋地向大家讲述上帝如何用一段简单的诗句, 从一段复杂的段落中, 他的故事是针对每个人的,但可能有一个特别的单词,可以和房间里的几个团体交谈. 一个是外行者,也就是在基督教部之外从事正常工作谋生的人。

没有神学院教育的人, 我们承认,这一系列的描述 4人谁是传道者。

现在,我们的系列有一个有趣的流传:首先,圣奥古斯丁, 然后,路德,他是一个奥古斯丁的修道士, 然后,约翰·邦扬,他最喜欢的书是路德对加拉提安的评论, 现在,查尔斯·斯普吉翁,他最喜欢的书是"邦扬朝圣者的进步"。

但我们系列的一个弱点(某种意义上的)就是他们都成了传教士。 我们并不期望你们都成为传教士;我们想做几个,但多数是外行,这很好。

现在,斯普吉翁被称为"道教的王子". 但是,在上帝的统治下,在斯普吉翁的故事里,英雄不是斯普吉翁,也不是一个受过训练,有报酬的传教士,而是一名外行人. 因此,斯普吉恩的故事有一个特别的词来形容那些愿意张开口子,说出自己对耶稣所了解的. Spurgeon的故事中也有一个针对青少年和年轻成年人的特殊词.

斯普吉安在15岁时开始信仰,在他这一天,这更像是年轻的成年. 然而,他的故事给那些已经不是孩子和还没有成年的人带来了挑战:青少年,大学生,研究生,甚至年轻专业人员.

不要让世界(或教会)降低你对于什么是可能的, 我的祷告是 上帝可能很乐意 给一些自己的引擎。 父母、大学员工和牧师经常帮助年轻的成年人并给予他们推动。

有时,上帝在青少年生活中很高兴给他们自己的引擎,他们不需要再再推了. 他们说:你们离我远点! 我要跟随耶稣。 你无法阻止我远离他, 这是上帝在15岁时为斯波克森所做的——他给了他自己的引擎. 我祈求他今天上午也乐意这么做

Spurgeon的故事又讲述了一个群体:那些在房间里愿意承认“我在这里,但我没有被拯救。 ” 两千年来,无所救护的人出于各种原因都出现在了教堂. 这是斯普吉恩的故事。 他在寻找。 周日早上,上帝破门而入时,他被解剖,在教堂里。

所以,如果你今天上午说,“我还没有解决我的罪恶和反抗上帝的问题,”或者“我还没有`拯救',或者“如果我今天在回家的路上死了,我也不会与我的造物主和睦相处,”这个故事有一个特别的词给你。 让我告诉你查理·斯波克森的事 他于1834年生于伦敦东北约40英里处,进入基督教家庭.

事实上,他的父亲和祖父都是牧师。 但是他的父亲遇到了财政上的困难,并派年轻的查尔斯从一到六岁就和外祖父母住在一起. 我并不认为这是故事的次要部分,

从他们的影响力中,他出现了“珍贵的,”学会了阅读,并首先发现了邦扬的"朝圣者进步"(他将读一百多遍)。 从他最初的年代起,他就异常尖锐地领先于他的年龄,"总是阅读书籍"("外科医生:一部传记",8). 他六岁回家,在学校数学和阅读方面都非常出色。

articles.summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第四个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。在基督徒的生活中，没有承诺或命令的危机经历是必不可少的元素。一些关于基督徒生活的教导断言， […]《基督徒生活中没有必要的危机经历》一文首先出现在《美国真理旗帜》上。
articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有必要的危机经历
articles.content: The fourth of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. There is no crisis experience promised or commanded as an essential element in living the Christian life. Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that only a low level of Christian experience can be realized by the person who has not had a crisis experience subsequent to regeneration, or at least subsequent to conversion and to the beginning of conscious Christian experience. Furthermore, it is asserted that the crisis experience is both commanded and promised by God as the entrance into a qualitatively new dimension or level of spiritual experience, reality and power. Throughout the history of the Christian church there have been many different strands of this crisis teaching. There is what we might call ‘classic Wesleyan perfectionism,’ which concentrated particularly upon sanctification and spoke of a baptism of purifying fire, or of coming into a state of perfect love. It concentrated not so much on power for service or upon inward feelings, but on a crisis experience in which the power of indwelling sin was to all intents and purposes negated. I have read enough of classic Wesleyan theology to know that there are different opinions as to what John Wesley himself taught on the subject. But in a general descriptive manner this, I believe, is an accurate representation of old-style classic Wesleyan perfectionism. Then, too, there is ‘the old Pentecostalism’ in which the emphasis was upon a baptism in the Holy Spirit, generally subsequent to conversion, and invariably manifested by speaking in tongues: the way you knew that you had this baptism of power was that, when it came to you, you spoke in tongues. The primary focus in old classic Pentecostalism was the matter of power for service. Thirdly, there is the modern ‘charismatic movement.’ Like classic Pentecostalism, its teachers use many of the same passages in the Book of Acts to support their theory of this necessary crisis. So they emphasize that in most cases—although there are different schools among modern charismatics—it will be manifested by the speaking in tongues. Some are content to believe you have ‘got it’ if you have a season of holy laughter. Others, however, say that you have not spoken in tongues because you have some psychological hold-ups, and if these can be removed the tongues are there. You just have not given them utterance. Here the emphasis is not so much on a baptism of purifying fire (as in the case of old classic Wesleyan perfectionism), or the baptism of power (as in the case of old classic Pentecostalism), but more upon a baptism of joyful praise-filled experience. I have been speaking of generalities, but I believe they are accurate. Fourthly, there are the various forms of ‘higher life’ teaching. What they have in common is this: you are simply converted, simply united to Christ, simply regenerated, and then you come to a crisis of surrender and faith, in which ‘you let go and let God’ and appropriate the indwelling life of Christ. The common denominator is that it is a crisis without any external manifestation of tongues or holy laughter or shouting or jumping, but the end result will be new power to live a holy life—the emphasis falls upon the ability to be more efficient in the path of holiness. Fifthly, there is a kind of teaching which has both old and modern proponents. It focuses on assurance, and has been expressed in terms of the biblical language of a ‘sealing of the Holy Spirit.’ Some of the Puritans—Thomas Goodwin, for example—taught this. There have been certain preachers in our own day who have believed this very strongly and emphasized it repeatedly. The basic concern in this teaching is that, subsequent to regeneration and conversion, there is a crisis experience in which the believer enters into a qualitatively new dimension of assurance by
articles.content_zh: 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年会议上发表的包含教学内容的六篇文章中的第四篇,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 没有任何危机经历作为过上基督教生活的一项基本要素得到承诺或接受。 一些关于基督教生活的教义主张,在再生后,或至少是在皈依后,以及自觉的基督教经历开始后,没有危机经历的人,只有低水平的基督教经验才能实现. 此外,有人断言,危机经历既是上帝的旨意,也是上帝的允诺,是精神经历、现实和力量进入一个全新的层面或层次的。 在基督教会的历史上,这种危机教育有许多不同的内容。 我们可能称之为“经典的卫斯理完美主义 ” , 它不是把精力集中在服务或内在感情上,而是集中在一种危机经历上,在这种经历中,罪恶的威力是所有意图和目的所否定的。 我读了足够多的经典的卫斯理神学,知道对于约翰·卫斯理自己教授的这个主题,有不同的看法. 但从一般的描述方式来看,我认为,这是对老式经典的卫斯理主义的准确表述. 也存在“五旬节派”的旧现象, 重点是圣灵中的洗礼, 通常是在皈依之后, 古老的经典五旬节主义的主要焦点是服务的权力问题. 第三,有现代`魅力运动'。 和经典的五旬节主义一样,它的老师们也用"行动书"中的许多同名段落来支持他们对这个必要危机的理论. 所以他们强调,在多数情况下,尽管现代魅力中存在着不同的学校,但用舌头说话将表明这一点。 如果你有一个圣笑的季节, 然而,其他人说,你没有说出舌头,因为你有一些心理障碍,如果这些障碍可以取出,舌头就在那里。 你只是没说 这里强调的不是净化火的洗礼(如旧经典的卫斯理完美主义),也不是权力的洗礼(如旧经典的五旬节主义),而是更强调充满欢乐的赞美经验的洗礼. 我一直在谈论泛泛而谈,但我认为它们是正确的。 第四,有各种形式的 " 更高的生活 " 教学。 他们的共同点是:你们只是皈依正教,只是与基督联合,只是再生,然后你们遭遇了投降和信仰的危机,你们在危机中“放手,放任真主出征”,而顺从基督永生。 共同的分母是,这是一场没有外在表现出舌头或圣笑或叫喊或跳跃的危机,但最终结果将是新的力量来过上圣生活——强调在圣道上更有效率的能力. 第五,有一种教学既有老的也有现代的支持者。 它侧重于保证,并用圣经中的"封圣"来表述. 一些清教徒——例如托马斯·古德温——教授了这个。 在我们这一天里,有一些传道者非常强烈地相信并反复强调这一点。 该教学的基本关注是,在再生和转生之后,存在着一种危机经历,信仰者通过下列方式进入了保证的质的新层面:

articles.content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. articles.title_zh: 为什么许多人自称基督，却不拥有基督--这对门徒意味着什么
articles.content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Moody Publishers and adapted from The Unstoppable Gospel by Karl Clauson. It’s impossible to disciple lost people. That sounds obvious. Maybe too obvious to even say out loud. But when the church dilutes or neglects the good news, devastation is left in its wake. After forty years of ministry, this is the most sobering truth I’ve learned about the Western church: We do not merely have a discipleship problem today. We have a gospel problem. Before we ever became weak at disciple-making, we began redefining conversion itself. We slowly traded supernatural regeneration for human decision. Salvation became a prayer to repeat, a card to sign, an aisle to walk, while millions were assured of heaven without ever being transformed by the power of God. We didn’t offer them a belief lacking power, we offered them a powerless belief. The result is a generation that has been deeply Christianized but not necessarily changed. They know the language. They know the songs. They know when to stand, when to sit, when to say amen. They have been immersed in church culture, yet many have never been brought from death to life. We have filled churches with people who have learned how to function in and around “Christianity” without ever truly following Christ. And when that happens, discipleship collapses under the weight of human effort. When evangelism centers on human decision, discipleship inevitably becomes self-powered. Following Jesus is reduced to behavior management, moral striving, and “try harder next time.” The supernatural life Christ promised is replaced with self-help dressed up in religious garb. Dallas Willard spoke of “the Great Omission,” the church’s failure to make disciples. He was right. But I believe something even deeper has happened. Before we omitted discipleship, we compromised the very gospel that births disciples in the first place. That is the crisis. That is the great deception. And until we recover the true faith that changes everything, we will continue trying to disciple people who have never truly been made alive. We have, sitting in our church chairs and pews every weekend—even in good, Bible-teaching churches—vast numbers of people who believe themselves to be saved but possess no power beyond their own efforts and whose lives show only surface evidence of new birth. People assume what they have is all God has for them, not knowing they are cultural Christians, so close yet so far from God. People who have been taught a version of Christianity divorced from repentance, from surrender, from the cost of discipleship and, tragically, from the power that makes the gospel unstoppable. Many profess Christ but don’t possess Christ. We’ve left people needing more, wanting more, and settling for too little. The great deception must end. There is life for the spiritually dead. There is surrender that leads to life instead of loss. There is repentance that produces the rhythm of a flourishing soul. There is discipline that flows from grace instead of fear or performance. And there is deep, liberating, unmistakable freedom when Christ becomes everything. This is why truth must be championed. Not as an idea, but as a reality that cuts, clarifies, and calls us forward. Because when truth becomes really clear, it doesn’t just inform you. It changes you. It brings you out of the fog, out of the confusion, out of the illusion—and into a life that is grounded, whole, and fully alive with God. This is the gospel that birthed the early church. This is the gospel that turned the world upside down. This is the gospel that sustains God’s kids under brutal persecution today. This is the gospel the church has forgotten and the good news it desperately needs. This is the gospel that still changes everything today. Learn more about how we’ve embraced a version of the gospel that falls short of the life Jesus promised, and how you can go from powerless belief to a true faith that changes everything. Get

博客由Mody出版社赞助, 门徒不可能失去人 这听起来很明显。 也许太明显了,甚至不能大声说出来。 但当教堂淡化或忽略了好消息时,毁灭就留在了它的后面.

这是40年的牧师, 我们今天不只是有门徒问题。 我们有一个福音问题。 在做门徒之前,我们开始重新定义皈依本身。 我们慢慢地用超自然再生来换取人类的决定。

救世主成为了重复的祷告,签字的名片,行走的走道,而数百万人则得到天堂的保证,永远没有被上帝的力量所改变. 我们并没有给他们一个没有权力的信仰, 其结果是一代人被深深地基督教化,但不一定改变. 他们知道语言。 他们知道歌曲。

他们知道何时可以站起,何时可以坐起,何时可以说阿门. 他们被浸入了教会文化中,然而许多人从未被从死亡中带入生命. 我们向教会灌输了那些学会如何在 " 基督教 " 内和周围运作而不真正遵循基督的人。 当这种情况发生时,门徒们在人类努力的重压下崩溃了.

当福音会以人类的决定为中心时,门徒不可避免地会变得自强自强. 追随耶稣被贬为行为管理、道德努力和“下次更努力”的人。 基督所承诺的超自然生命被取而代之的是身穿宗教外衣的自救. Dallas Willard谈到了教会未能培养出门徒的“大意念”。 他说得对。

但我相信发生了更深层的事 在我们忽略了门徒身份之前,我们破坏了出生的门徒们最初的福音。 这就是危机。 这是伟大的欺骗。 直到我们恢复改变一切的真正信仰之前,我们将继续尝试向从未真正被活生生地培养出来的门徒.

我们每个周末都坐在教堂的椅子上和教堂的树上,即使是好的,也是圣经教学的教堂。 我们有许多人相信自己是被拯救的,但除了自己的努力之外没有权力,他们的生活只显示新出生的表面证据。 人们猜想自己拥有的只是上帝给他们的一切,他们不知道自己是文化上的基督徒,所以距离上帝还相去甚远.

曾被教过基督教的人脱离了忏悔、投降、门徒费用以及可悲的使福音无法被阻止的力量。 许多人信奉基督, 我们让人们需要更多,需要更多, 伟大的欺骗必须结束。 精神上死去的人有生命

投降导致生命而不是损失。 有悔过感产生出一个繁荣的灵魂的节奏. 纪律是从优雅而不是恐惧或表现中产生的。 当基督变成一切时,有深刻的,解放的,不可磨灭的自由. 这就是为什么必须捍卫真理。 不是作为一个想法,而是作为一个现实,削减、澄清和召唤我们前进。

因为当真相变得非常清楚时, 它改变了你。 它使你从雾中、从迷惑中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻雾中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻幻觉中、从幻幻觉中、从幻幻出出,进入一个与神同活生。 这是诞生早期教堂的福音. 这就是使世界颠倒的福音。

这是上帝孩子今天遭受残酷迫害的福音。 这是教堂被遗忘的福音 也是它急需的好消息 这是今天仍然改变一切的福音。

articles.title_zh: 很遗憾地通知您，天堂旅游又回来了
articles.content: I regret to inform you, dear reader, that heaven tourism is back. The genre possibly never went away entirely, but it did at least disappear from the bestseller lists for several years. Sadly, it has returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven , which was one of the bestselling Christian books last month and even made its way to the New York Times list of bestsellers—a feat most authors can only dream of. Out of sheer magnanimity (and perhaps a morbid sense of curiosity), I read it so you don’t have to. 18 Days in Heaven Gabe Poirot Before I tell you what it’s all about, here’s a brief history of heaven tourism. Don Piper kicked off the genre in 2004 with 90 Minutes in Heaven , and it proved a surprise hit that quickly dominated the sales charts, eventually tallying upwards of 8 million copies sold. Todd Burpo’s Heaven Is for Real followed in 2010 with over 10 million copies sold. That same year brought Kevin and Alex Malarkey’s The Boy Who Came Back from Heaven , which sold more than a million copies before Alex recanted his story and the publisher pulled it. The genre went on to deliver many more heaven books and a handful of less-popular hell books like Bill Wiese’s 23 Minutes in Hell , though none ever reached the same heights as the first few—no pun intended. My contribution to the genre was little more than reviewing several of the books and coining the snarky phrase “heaven tourism,” which, much to my delight, soon caught on . The genre inevitably ran its course, but has now returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven: I Left My Body. I Met Jesus. What He Told Me Will Alter Your Eternity . Sadly, but not surprisingly, it is just as bad as its predecessors, mixing truth with errors and documented facts with spurious speculations until it is as confusing and unreliable as any of them. 18 Days in Heaven follows the standard pattern by beginning with an account of a terrible accident—in this case, a head injury that resulted from a skateboarding mishap. Poirot, a young evangelist with a sizable YouTube following, was rendered comatose and remained hovering between life and death for 18 days. But while his body was inert, his soul was transported to heaven, where it experienced heavenly wonders, not the least of which was spending time with Jesus. What did he see and experience there? Many things, of course, some of which he is able to describe and many of which he insists he cannot, either because God told him not to or because they defy description. What can he describe? Jesus’s eyes, in which “I saw all the colors that had ever existed or could exist, all in one. He was the deepest ocean of liquid love that had no end. A spectrum of intensity that only increased the longer I stared. His eyebrows, hair, jawline, arms, chest, heart, stature, ears, forehead, eyelashes, teeth, mouth, skin, and complexion all said the same thing: I love you, I love you, I love you.” He describes Jesus’s scars which “were like an ocean that had no floor,” and had the name “Gabriel” written immediately above them. He learned from them that Jesus has completely and eternally forgotten his sins so that he could no longer remember them even if he wanted to. He smelled Jesus and observed that his “fragrance wasn’t like the humidity of the Florida Everglades. No, this was something eternal—an everlasting fountain of fire, not just surrounding me but burning into me. Wrapping around me like a robe, like a living garment of pure, unending presence. It felt burning hot and freezing cold at the same time.” He heard Jesus say many words and noted that his “words were not just a separate entity that He ‘released.’ They were like the sharpest spears that went right into the core of my very being. But these spears were not separate from Him—they were Him.” Poirot even saw his own conception: “The light from Father God united with the earthly seed from my father and the egg of my mother in that moment, and I began my existence on earth. I was not born just on
articles.content_zh:
我很遗憾地告诉你,亲爱的读者 天堂旅游又回来了 流派可能从未完全消失,但至少从畅销书榜上消失了几年.

不幸的是,它回到了Gabe Poirot的"天堂18天"中,这是上个月最畅销的基督教书籍之一,甚至走进了纽约时报畅销书榜,这是大多数作者只能梦想的功绩。 我读了这篇文章,

同年,凯文和亚历克丝·马拉克的"从天堂回来的男孩"(The Boy Who Came from Heaven)也带来了,后者在亚历克丝收回他的故事并被出版商拉出之前就售出超过一百万份. 虽然没有人能达到与前几本书相同的高度,

我对这个流派的贡献不过是回顾几本书, 但现在又回到了Gabe Poirot在天堂的18天:我离开了我的身体。 我遇见了耶稣。 他告诉我 Will 改变你的永恒

可悲但并不令人惊讶的是,它同其前身一样糟糕,把事实与错误相混淆,把有记录的事实同虚假的猜测相混淆,直到它同其中任何一个都一样令人困惑和不可靠。 18天的"天堂"遵循了标准模式,首先讲述了一起可怕的事故——在此情况下,由于滑板出事而造成头部受伤.

Poirot是一位年轻的福音传播者,他带着一个庞大的YouTube跟随,因此被昏迷并徘徊在生与死之间长达18天. 但虽然他的身体是惰性的,他的灵魂被运到了天堂,在那里它经历了天堂的奇事,其中最起碼是和耶稣一起度过. 他在那里看到了什么? 体验什么?

当然,许多事情,有些是他能够描述的,有些是他坚持不能描述的,要么是因为上帝告诉他不要描述,要么是因为他们藐视描述。 他能描述什么? 耶稣的眼睛,其中,“我看到了曾经存在或可能存在的所有颜色,都是一种颜色。 他是无尽的液体爱最深的海洋

强度的光谱 只会增加我恒星的长度 他的眉毛、发型、下巴、手臂、胸部、心、身高、耳朵、额头、睫毛、牙齿、口腔、皮肤和相貌都说了同样的话:我爱你,我爱你,我爱你。” 他描述了耶稣的伤疤,这些伤疤 " 像一片没有地的海洋 " ,上面写有 " Gabriel " 的名字。

他从他们那里得知,耶稣已经彻底地,永远地忘记了自己的罪过,这样即使他愿意也再也记不住了. 他闻到耶稣的气味并观察到他的"香气不像佛罗里达埃弗格拉德河的湿润. 不,这是永恒的东西, 一个永恒的火焰喷泉, 不仅包围着我,而且燃烧在我身上。

缠绕我就像长袍一样 像纯洁无尽的活衣 它同时感到被烧得发热而冷冻。” 他听到耶稣说出许多话,并指出他的"词不仅是一个他‘释放'的独立实体. 他们就像最锋利的长矛 直入我生命的核心

这些长矛,不是与他分开的,他们确是他。 波洛甚至看到了自己的构想:“神父所赐的光与我父亲所赐的地上种子和母亲的卵合而为一,我开始了我在地上的存在。 我不是刚出生
